title: Grease both Robotiq Hand-E racks into their guide-flange steps while keeping the tapped faces dry
keywords: hold a small part against a brush
instruction: Grease both racks with the brush for reassembly: every surface except the face with the tapped holes (the small end faces may stay bare), keeping the brush off the opened gripper and its parts. Then leave the racks in the tray and the brush back across it.
context: Robotics technicians service the Robotiq Hand-E rack-and-pinion mechanism every 2 million cycles, sooner in dirty conditions (maker maintenance procedure, section 6.3). Before reassembly, grease must cover the sliding faces and recessed flange steps while tapped mounting faces stay dry. This tests selective coating of loose precision parts: one hand steadies the brush on the tray rims while the other presents a rack, without wiping finished surfaces or carrying grease onto the mounting face.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table. A grey anti-static bench mat, 457 x 610 x 2 (18 x 24 in), centre x 300, y 0. On it a Miltex non-perforated Mayo instrument tray, stainless steel, 254 x 165 x 18 (10 x 6-1/2 x 23/32 in), long side along x, centre x 300, y 0; its floor is 3 above the table. In the tray, lying along y with the tapped face up: the two steel racks of a Robotiq Hand-E gripper (HND-GRP), taken out of its rack housing, degreased and dried. Each is 62 long with a cross-shaped section from the maker's Fig. 5-11: a lower stem 6.1 wide x 4.8 tall (its underside is the back), a guide flange 14.0 x 6.0 and an upper stem 6.1 x 5.3 whose top is the tapped face (three M3 tapped holes and two 2 mm dowel holes); teeth along one side of the lower stem; 71 g. The length, the stem and flange heights and the mass are estimates read off the drawing. Rack 1 at x 270, y 30; rack 2 at x 210, y 30. A reusable nylon brush replica with a tile-and-grout-style handle, 248 long, 60 g (estimate): handle 22 x 183 x 12, head 25 x 65 x 12, nylon bristles 22 long in a 20 x 56 block (block, head and handle sizes estimated), loaded by hand with about 1 g of red Mobilith SHC 1500 grease. It lies bristles up across the tray's two long walls at x 320, head over the +y wall (head middle at y 60), handle toward -y. Fixed on the mat beyond the tray: the opened Hand-E body (rack housing off, pinion showing; 75 base, 83 tall) standing at x 490, y 170; its rack housing (75 x 16) lying at x 490, y 68; its coupling GRP-ES-CPL-062 (75 x 16.9) at x 490, y -35; the ACC-LUB-SHC1500 grease syringe (about 22 x 120) lying along y at x 470, y -150. Lot B mirrors lot A across y = 0: the brush turned end for end (head over the -y wall, handle toward +y) and the racks at y -30. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Real-trial kit: two reusable steel rack replicas machined once to the section above, with three M3 holes in the top face; dimensioned brush replica; stock tray, mat and grease; printed or wooden replicas of the fixed body, housing and coupling; a 20 mL plastic syringe. Estimated kit budget US$335, excluding robot, cameras and measuring tools (itemized in the README). Match the rack section, mass and bristle envelope before enrolment. Reset uses wipes and a fresh 1 g grease load; allow 3-5 minutes as a planning estimate, subject to the clean-tissue checks.
scoring: Read from the overhead and wrist videos and, after the trial, square-on photos of each rack's back, both sides and tapped face with a transparent 1 mm grid held beside the rack (the supplied 1:1 rack stencil lays out the 16 windows along each face and the strips across it). Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: any grease reaches a tapped face (a white tissue pressed on it comes away red); a rack lands on the mat or the table outside the tray; the bristles touch the opened gripper, its rack housing, its coupling or the syringe. A window is greased if red grease shows in it (simulation: part of it lies inside the bristles' outline while the brush presses that rack with 0.2 N or more and moves against it at 3 mm/s or more, 2 mm in all). A finger or gripper that touches a greased window wipes it bare, and a greasy finger that touches a tapped face puts grease on it. Zones of each rack: the back (back face in three strips across, the lower stem's two sides, the flange's two undersides: 112 windows) and each side (flange side, flange top, upper stem side: 48); a zone is greased at 90% of its windows. The two small end faces are not scored. Every score needs, for the last 1 s, both racks lying in the tray (inside its walls, lowest point within 3 mm of the floor), both hands at least 30 mm from the racks and the brush, and everything still. 1.0: all six zones greased and the brush lying across the tray's two long walls, bristles up, between its short walls. 0.75: all six zones. 0.5: all three zones of one rack. 0.25: at least two zones. 0 otherwise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: Reuse the same two steel racks or replicas and brush; no new specimen or cure between trials. Allow 3-5 minutes for reset (planning estimate, not measured). 1. Wipe grease from racks, tray and finger-pad covers with compatible degreaser; dry fully. Press a fresh white tissue on every rack face and both end-grip areas: no red transfer before enrolment. Replace contaminated pad covers and clean the brush handle. 2. Place racks along y, tapped faces up, at x 270 and x 210; both y 30 for lot A, y -30 for B. 3. Remove old excess grease from the bristles, then work in a fresh 1 g load with a spatula; weigh the added grease rather than assuming 1 g equals 1 mL. 4. Lay the brush bristles up across both long tray walls at x 320, head over +y for A or -y for B. Check the handle and fixed obstacles with fresh white tissues: no red transfer. Continue cleaning if any check fails. Grease, wipes and contaminated pad covers are consumed; specimens, brush and obstacles are reused.
fidelity: Isaac Sim/PhysX rigid bodies, 20 Hz. Rack section is based on Robotiq Fig. 5-11; length, section heights and mass are estimates. Brush is a dimensioned replica, not a measured Libman 18: 20 x 56 x 22 mm bristle envelope around a 10 x 46 x 17 mm contact core. Grease coverage uses contact-force and motion rules; fingers wipe and transfer it. No fluid flow, film thickness or tray transfer. Teeth and holes are visual only. The 0.2 N threshold and bristle response are uncalibrated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (A 0.0, B 0.0; 2,400-step limit, no refusal; the arms stayed near their bases and touched nothing). Demo: 1.0 in A and B (all six zones greased, both tapped faces dry, racks back in the tray, brush on the rims, hands clear and still; success at 1,904 steps).
